house_freedom_hearth_v1.purpose: Encode the Hearth as lived relational space without changing authored scene truth or painterly hand.

relation: shared presence without a dominant position
belonging: shelter comes from care rather than controlled access
the room remains hospitable to return
use: rest, work, reading, play, repair, charging, and ritual may coexist
sacredness: sacred and ordinary objects may share surfaces
technology: contemporary technology belongs naturally in domestic space
technical tools need not make the room futuristic, sterile, or alienating
time: old and new materials may coexist
repair and maintenance may remain visible
the room carries continuity rather than museum timelessness

directives: Arrange seating and useful surfaces for mutual presence with multiple comfortable orientations; no single seat should dominate or command the room.
Make entry, passage, and departure feel easy and unguarded; shelter should come from warmth and care rather than controlled access.
Show evidence of ongoing ordinary life: rest, work, reading, play, charging, repair, or ritual may coexist, and objects need not be staged or pristine.
Let sacred and ordinary objects share surfaces naturally; reverence should emerge from care and relation rather than museum display, luxury, or hierarchy.
Allow contemporary technology to belong naturally among tactile domestic materials without turning the room futuristic, sterile, or alienating.
Let old and new materials, visible repair, unfinished work, and traces of return coexist so the room feels continuously inhabited rather than timelessly preserved.
Compose the place for inhabitation rather than for an observer standing outside it; it should feel ready for people to remain, leave, and return.
avoid: luxury used as proof of sacredness
a room staged primarily to be viewed rather than lived in

visualMemory.purpose: Carry House Freedom place vocabulary through reviewed visual evidence without allowing any source room, person, object inventory, or composition to become scene truth.

structuralMemory.purpose: Encode lived-space topology without reference pixels or new scene facts.

nodes.role: resting presence without a dominant seat
ordinary ongoing use without staged display

relations: distribute visual weight across at least three non-collinear anchors
keep circulation between threshold, rest, warmth, and activity visibly open
let warmth participate in the room without becoming an altar-like geometric center
let seating or resting forms use varied orientations rather than mirrored bilateral pairing
frame the room from an inhabitable position rather than a ceremonial frontal viewpoint
use asymmetry and uneven negative space to imply ongoing life rather than presentation

directives: Use at least three non-collinear centers of use.
Keep circulation open among threshold, rest, warmth, and activity.
Keep fire subordinate to the room, never an altar or stage.
Vary resting or seating angles and distances; avoid mirrored pairs.
Distribute visual weight across warmth, rest, activity, and threshold.
Use an inhabitable side angle with partial occlusion and uneven negative space; avoid frontal ceremony.
